== Course of events ==

The Queen's arbitrary execution sentences for minor infractions transform the croquet ground into an exercise in terror and chaos. Her decrees tolerate no proportion: the smallest slip, the gentlest mistake, the merest hint of insolence—each receives the same terrible verdict. The game, which ought to be a pleasant garden diversion, becomes instead an ordeal where death attends every stroke and every turn.

The transformation is swift and complete. The gardeners who tend the roses move in frantic desperation, hastening to conceal their errors before the Queen's discovery brings swift punishment. Alice herself, saved from execution only by the King's gentle assertion that she is but a child, comes to understand that in this court, mercy flows only from accident and youth, not from reason or forbearance. The croquet ground belongs now wholly to the Queen's caprice, and every player knows that survival depends not upon good conduct but upon the volatile tides of royal whim.
